Parallel Python Workers with condathis and mizu

Source: vignettes/articles/python-and-mizu.qmd

Python Workers Next to Your R Session

run() starts a fresh python for every call, and data moves through files and standard streams. reticulate embeds one interpreter in the R process. The mizu package sits between the two:

  • It starts a pool of Python processes once, and they stay alive between tasks.
  • R vectors, matrices and data frames reach the workers through shared memory. Large objects are not copied.
  • Tasks run in the background. The R session stays free until you collect the results.
  • A crash in a worker does not end your R session.

condathis provides the interpreter and the packages of the workers. This article needs the mizu R package, and the pymizu Python package in the environment. The mizu API is still marked experimental.

Creating the Environment

pymizu is published on PyPI, not on conda-forge. An environment YAML file installs it with pip, after micromamba installs the Conda packages. env_definition() passes the file to create_env().

env_file <- fs::file_temp(pattern = "py-mizu-", ext = "yml")

writeLines(
  con = env_file,
  text = c(
    "channels:",
    "  - conda-forge",
    "dependencies:",
    "  - python=3.13",
    "  - numpy",
    "  - pandas",
    "  - pyarrow",
    "  - pip",
    "  - pip:",
    "      - pymizu==0.1.1"
  )
)

create_env(
  env_definition(env_file),
  env_name = "py-mizu-env",
  verbose = "silent"
)

list_packages() lists the pip package with the channel pypi.

pkgs <- list_packages(env_name = "py-mizu-env", verbose = "silent")
pkgs[pkgs$name %in% c("python", "numpy", "pymizu"), c("name", "version", "channel")]
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   name   version channel    
#>   <chr>  <chr>   <chr>      
#> 1 numpy  2.5.5   conda-forge
#> 2 pymizu 0.1.1   pypi       
#> 3 python 3.13.18 conda-forge

Starting a Pool

mizu_py_launcher() starts the workers with a given Python interpreter. It checks that pymizu imports in that interpreter, so a missing package fails here and not later in a task.

The launcher starts python directly, without the environment’s activation. On Windows, compiled packages then fail to find their DLLs in the environment’s Library\bin folder. env_launcher() below asks the activated environment for the interpreter path and for PATH, and sets that PATH only while the workers start.

library(mizu)

env_launcher <- function(env_name) {
  info <- parse_output(
    run(
      "python", "-c",
      "import os, sys; print(sys.executable); print(os.environ['PATH'])",
      env_name = env_name,
      verbose = "silent"
    )
  )
  launch <- mizu_py_launcher(python = info[[1]])

  function(token, slot) {
    old_path <- Sys.getenv("PATH")
    on.exit(Sys.setenv(PATH = old_path))
    Sys.setenv(PATH = info[[2]])
    if (missing(slot)) launch(token) else launch(token, slot)
  }
}

mizu_pool() starts two workers.

pool <- mizu_pool(n_workers = 2L, launcher = env_launcher("py-mizu-env"))

The workers get the activated PATH, but no other activation variables. If a package needs a variable from an activate.d script, set it with Sys.setenv() before you start the pool.

Calling Python Functions

mizu_call() names a Python function and its arguments. mizu_submit_call() sends it to the pool and returns at once. mizu_collect() waits for the result.

task <- mizu_submit_call(
  pool,
  mizu_call("numpy.quantile", faithful$eruptions, q = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
)

mizu_collect(task)
#> [1] 2.16275 4.00000 4.45425

An R numeric vector arrives as a NumPy array. NA arrives as a missing value and comes back as NA.

Running Python Code

With .source, the task is a piece of Python code. The named arguments become Python variables, and the value of the last line is the result.

A data frame arrives as a pymizu.Frame. pyarrow.table() reads it without a copy, and to_pandas() converts it to a pandas data frame. A pandas data frame comes back as an R data frame.

summarize_py <- "
import pyarrow as pa
df = pa.table(cars).to_pandas()
df.groupby('cyl')[['mpg', 'hp']].mean().reset_index()
"

task <- mizu_submit_call(
  pool,
  mizu_call(.source = summarize_py, cars = mtcars)
)

mizu_collect(task)
#>   cyl      mpg        hp
#> 1   4 26.66364  82.63636
#> 2   6 19.74286 122.28571
#> 3   8 15.10000 209.21429

Factor columns cross as factors, in both directions. Some R types cannot cross, such as functions, formulas and S4 objects. mizu raises an error when you send one.

Working in the Background

Each submission returns before the task finishes. Submit several tasks, continue in R, and collect them all when you need the results. The two workers run the tasks in parallel.

slow_py <- "
import os, time
time.sleep(1)
os.getpid()
"

tasks <- lapply(1:4, function(i) {
  mizu_submit_call(pool, mizu_call(.source = slow_py))
})

# The R session is free while the workers sleep
invisible(sum(seq_len(1e6)))

system.time({
  pids <- mizu_collect_all(tasks)
})
#>    user  system elapsed 
#>     0.0     0.0     1.9
table(unlist(pids))
#> 
#> 13581 13583 
#>     2     2

Four one-second tasks take about two seconds on two workers. Each worker process ran two of them.

mizu_map() applies one Python function to every element of a vector, and splits the work across the pool.

log_waiting <- mizu_map(
  pool,
  faithful$waiting[1:6],
  mizu_call("numpy.log"),
  .template = numeric(1)
)

mizu_collect(log_waiting)
#> [1] 4.369448 3.988984 4.304065 4.127134 4.442651 4.007333

Large Data in Shared Memory

mizu writes a large object to shared memory once, without serializing it. The worker reads the values in place. Ten million doubles, 80 MB, reach Python in a fraction of a second.

x <- stats::rnorm(1e7)

system.time({
  py_sd <- mizu_collect(mizu_submit_call(pool, mizu_call("numpy.std", x)))
})
#>    user  system elapsed 
#>   0.010   0.007   0.030

all.equal(py_sd, stats::sd(x), tolerance = 1e-6)
#> [1] TRUE

NumPy’s std() divides by n and R’s sd() by n - 1. With ten million values, the difference is below the tolerance.

Handling Python Errors

A Python exception in a task becomes an R error of class mizu_error_remote when you collect the task. The message holds the Python exception. The worker keeps running and accepts more tasks.

task <- mizu_submit_call(pool, mizu_call(.source = "import not_installed_module"))

tryCatch(mizu_collect(task), mizu_error_remote = conditionMessage)
#> [1] "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'not_installed_module'"

Pools from Several Environments

Each pool uses the interpreter of one environment. Pools from different environments can run at the same time, with different Python versions and package sets. This environment has Python 3.12 and scikit-learn.

ml_env_file <- fs::file_temp(pattern = "py-mizu-ml-", ext = "yml")

writeLines(
  con = ml_env_file,
  text = c(
    "channels:",
    "  - conda-forge",
    "dependencies:",
    "  - python=3.12",
    "  - scikit-learn",
    "  - pandas",
    "  - pyarrow",
    "  - pip",
    "  - pip:",
    "      - pymizu==0.1.1"
  )
)

create_env(
  env_definition(ml_env_file),
  env_name = "py-mizu-ml-env",
  verbose = "silent"
)

ml_pool <- mizu_pool(n_workers = 1L, launcher = env_launcher("py-mizu-ml-env"))

Ask both pools for their Python version.

version_py <- "
import platform
platform.python_version()
"

c(
  data = mizu_collect(mizu_submit_call(pool, mizu_call(.source = version_py))),
  ml = mizu_collect(mizu_submit_call(ml_pool, mizu_call(.source = version_py)))
)
#>      data        ml 
#> "3.13.18" "3.12.16"

The scikit-learn pool clusters the faithful data frame. The labels come back as an R vector.

kmeans_py <- "
import pyarrow as pa
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
df = pa.table(points).to_pandas()
KMeans(n_clusters=2, n_init='auto', random_state=1).fit_predict(df)
"

clusters <- mizu_collect(
  mizu_submit_call(ml_pool, mizu_call(.source = kmeans_py, points = faithful))
)

table(clusters)
#> clusters
#>   0   1 
#> 172 100

Stopping the Pools

mizu_pool_stop() stops the workers and frees the shared memory.

mizu_pool_stop(pool)
mizu_pool_stop(ml_pool)

Choosing an Approach

Need Use
One-off scripts, crash safety, no extra R packages run()
Python objects kept in memory between calls, Python chunks reticulate
Persistent Python workers, parallel tasks, large R data mizu
R code next to Python in each process, other machines reticulate in mirai daemons

The article Running Python Code with condathis and reticulate shows the first, second and last approaches.

Cleaning Up 

remove_env(env_name = "py-mizu-env")
#> ✔ Environment py-mizu-env successfully removed.
remove_env(env_name = "py-mizu-ml-env")
#> ✔ Environment py-mizu-ml-env successfully removed.
